devctl.calib_note: Makes every cuvette holder report the same count from the same LED.
devctl.calib_step1: Load every holder the same way. All empty, or the same blank cuvette moved into each slot — whatever is left different between the holders is what gets divided out.
devctl.calib_step2: One LED colour per pass. The sensor's response depends on wavelength, so channels under different LEDs read orders of magnitude apart and cannot be scaled onto each other. If this instrument mixes colours, untick the others in Active channels and do one group at a time — factors of unticked channels are kept.
devctl.calib_step3: Check the light level. On the device's Raw Count screen, set gain and integration time until no channel reads OVFL.
devctl.calib_step_press: Press Calibrate now. Takes a few seconds. A refusal names the channel: different LED means it belongs to another group, anything else means that slot needs attention — a dark LED, an empty holder, or a cuvette left behind.
devctl.calib_step4: Copy the array into configuration.json on the CIRCUITPY drive. The device cannot write that file itself, so the factors are lost on the next power cycle until you do.
devctl.calib_step5: Run it again after the instrument is moved or re-lamped, or if it has sat unused: LED output falls with age.
devctl.calib_caveat: This does not change Absorbance or Transmittance — each channel is already divided by its own blank, which cancels the factor. It changes Raw Count, Irradiance, and any comparison between holders. If absorbance still disagrees between holders afterwards, the cause is elsewhere: pathlength, cuvette orientation, scattering, or a blank taken through different contents.
devctl.calib_need_channels: This device has only one active channel. Calibration scales the channels onto each other, so it needs at least two — add one in Active channels above, or in configuration.json.
devctl.calib_unsaved: Not saved — the device will lose these at the next power cycle.
devctl.calib_no_drive: No CIRCUITPY drive mounted — the factors cannot be saved and will be lost at the next power cycle.
devctl.calib_save_failed: The factors could not be saved to the device
devctl.channels_failed: The device refused that channel set

hint.devctl_calib_run: Measure every active channel now and scale them onto a common reference. Takes a few seconds.

hint.devctl_calib_save: Write these factors into configuration.json on the device's drive. The device restarts and comes back running them.
settings.device_link: Connect to the device when the panel is open
devctl.calib_note_manual: Scales what this instrument counts, so it agrees with the one you calibrated against.
devctl.calib_m_step1: Measure a reference on an instrument you trust — the same sample, the same cuvette, the same light.
devctl.calib_m_step2: Read the same sample here on the device's Raw Count screen, with gain and integration time set so nothing reads OVFL.
devctl.calib_m_step3: Divide. factor = reference counts ÷ counts read here. Type it below and press Apply — the range is 0.1 to 10.
devctl.calib_m_step4: Save to device to keep it. The device cannot write its own configuration.json, so the factor is lost on the next power cycle until you do.
devctl.calib_caveat_manual: This does not change Absorbance or Transmittance — each reading is divided by a blank taken through the same factor, which cancels it, and the blank in memory is rescaled when the factor changes so that stays true mid-run. It changes counts: Raw Count, Irradiance, and any comparison against another instrument.
devctl.calib_range: a factor must be between 0.1 and 10
hint.devctl_calib_apply: Send these factors to the device. They take effect immediately and last until the next power cycle, or until you save them.
